notes:
Context: QuickByte Studio builds an IDE plugin (VS Code & JetBrains) focused on ultra-low-latency inline completions and long-form code assistance. Looking to replace their in-house serverless inference with Redwood for predictable TTFT and streaming support.

Key excerpts / rep notes:
- CTO: "If first token doesn't show within ~120ms users complain — goal 80-120ms TTFT for single-line completions."
- Eng lead: prefer WebSocket bi-directional streaming for incremental tokens and fine-grained cancelation; SSE acceptable as fallback.
- Product: jitter (P95 variance) must be <30ms to avoid perceived stutter when typing. Need metrics in console.
- Backpressure: client should be able to cancel and debounce active requests, server should provide explicit partial-completion signals so UI can render and then resume.
- Token budget strategy: per-request cap (default 128 tokens) + server-side budgeting for multi-turn context; dynamic budget hooks (client hints when doing short completion vs full refactor).
- Model/version pinning: require ability to pin stable model for GA, plus canary rollouts to newer quantized variants. Must support automatic fallback to smaller quantized model when latency SLOs breach or GPU contention increases.
- Cost sensitivity: heavy daily active users (10k DAU) with high QPS bursts during dev sprints — want batching, prefix/KV cache reuse and intelligent routing to control token unit costs.
- Security: SSO + audit logging mandatory for enterprise customers; KMS integration for secret handling. EU customers require data residency.

Ask to Redwood: POC checklist (priority):
1) End-to-end integration sample: VS Code extension + WebSocket streaming to Redwood hosted endpoint.
2) TTFT baseline run: measure P50/P95 first-token latency under 50/100/200 concurrent completions.
3) Jitter test: quantify P95 variance; demo console charts.
4) Token-budget tuning guide: recommended defaults for inline vs long-form completions and sample prompt templates.
5) Pricing simulation for expected 10k DAU and 100 req/s bursts.

Quotes from demo: "We need streaming that feels instantaneous — not a second-long flush." — Senior PM.

Notes on integration ideas / engineering notes (shorthand):
- Keep local debounce 40ms; cancel inflight on new keystroke; reuse partial buffer when resuming.
- Use short-lived model-variant for low-latency hot-path; fallback to larger non-streaming for deep codegen.
- KV cache reuse across related editor buffers (same repo/file) to reduce context window token cost.
- Prefer small quantized models for cold-start/initial token, then switch to larger model for finalization if budget allows.
- Need SDK examples for incremental token commits and explicit close() for backpressure handling.

Decision signals: POC performance (TTFT + jitter) + clear pricing projection + ability to pin versions and auto-fallback.
